sources.title: China’s industrial profit growth fastest in five months as recovery remains uneven
Indonesia bourse sanctions five companies over shareholder data
New Zealand’s ruling coalition falls just short of majority, needs centrist Opportunity to govern

stories.topic: CHINA / INDUSTRIAL PROFITS / ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE / EQUITIES / ECONOMIC DATA
stories.headline: China’s October industrial profit growth reaches 20.1%, with an uneven recovery
stories.body: Reuters reported Chinese industrial firms’ October profits rising 20.1% year on year. January–October profit growth was 16% year on year, a cumulative measure distinct from the single-month rate. Artificial intelligence (AI)-related manufacturing remained stronger than businesses exposed to weak domestic demand. The figures do not establish a broad recovery in consumption or property. Equity-index moves shown in the source dashboard are omitted from this preview because their individual observation times and attribution were not independently reviewed.
stories.analysis: A strong aggregate profit reading can conceal sector weakness. Its implications for monetary easing depend on the breadth and persistence of the recovery.
stories.watch_next: Domestic demand, export growth, AI investment and People’s Bank of China policy.

stories.topic: INDONESIA / MSCI / EQUITIES / SHAREHOLDER DISCLOSURE / FREE FLOAT / GOVERNANCE
stories.headline: Indonesia’s exchange penalises five listed companies over shareholder-data discrepancies
stories.body: Reuters reported the Indonesia Stock Exchange penalising five listed companies after they failed to clarify or correct discrepancies in controlling-shareholder information and monthly ownership reports. The exchange did not specify the penalties. This is an enforcement development; it is not a completed MSCI reclassification, proof of passive-fund outflows or a verified isolated share-price reaction.
stories.analysis: Ownership transparency matters for index eligibility and investor confidence. Regulatory sanctions and any later index decision remain separate actions.
stories.watch_next: Corrective ownership disclosures and MSCI’s subsequent assessment.
stories.earlier: Retained v1 covered Indonesia’s MSCI-related market risks; v2 added MSCI’s clarification that its reclassification proposal remained under review. This v3 adds the exchange’s enforcement action. The source’s new sanctions-story alias is reconciled to that retained transparency event rather than duplicating its history.

stories.topic: NEW ZEALAND / NZD / CHRISTOPHER LUXON / ELECTIONS / FISCAL POLICY
stories.headline: New Zealand’s ruling coalition falls one seat short of a parliamentary majority
stories.body: Reuters reported final election results giving Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s ruling centre-right coalition in New Zealand 65 of 130 parliamentary seats, against the 66 required for a majority. The Opportunity Party won seven seats, and its leader said she would negotiate with National first. A coalition or confidence-and-supply agreement had not been completed. The final count changes the preliminary result; it does not establish the eventual governing agreement. No numerical NZD quotation is included in this preview.
stories.analysis: Government formation creates uncertainty over fiscal policy and currency sentiment; seat counts do not establish a financial-market return.
stories.watch_next: Coalition or confidence-and-supply negotiations and any confirmed agreement.
